v1_rows.answer: You have 30 days from the date of discharge to submit a main reimbursement claim [1][2], while the 2024 archived rules state a deadline of 15 days from discharge [3]. Additionally, group corporate plans allow a window of 60 days from discharge [5].

No, maternity is not covered on the Bronze plan [1][2].

Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns as of 1 April 2026 [1].

No, you cannot claim for IVF treatment, as it is listed as a permanent treatment-related exclusion [1].

If you are not satisfied with the Stage 1 outcome or receive no response within 15 days, you can escalate to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer (Stage 2) [2]. If Aurora's final response is still unsatisfactory, or if they have not responded within 30 days of the original complaint, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region (Stage 3) [1].

Aurora Health Insurance provides road ambulance cover of ₹5,000 per hospitalisation [1]. Additionally, the Gold plan includes an air ambulance cover of ₹2,50,000 per policy year, within India, on prior authorisation [5].

Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness, as required by the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 [1]. The 30-day initial waiting period applies, but no separate waiting period is required [1].

The free-look period is the window in which a new policy can be returned for a refund [3]. It lasts for 15 days from the receipt of the policy document (or 30 days for policies sold through distance marketing) [1][2].
You receive 150 wellness points for completing an annual health check-up [1].

A day-care procedure is a procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation because of technological advance, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [3]. Out-patient treatment is not considered a day-care procedure [3].
A hospital must notify Aurora of an emergency admission for cashless within **24 hours** of admission [1][5].
No, Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a Third Party Administrator (TPA) [1].
To qualify as a hospital under the policy, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or 15 in-patient beds elsewhere [1].

No, not everything will be paid [1][5]. Because your room rent of ₹15,000 per day exceeds your Silver limit of 2% (or ₹10,000 per day) for a ₹5,00,000 sum insured, a proportionate deduction applies to eligible heads, resulting in a total payable amount of ₹1,95,000 out of ₹2,80,000 billed [1][2][5].

Dependent parents can be covered on Silver (at an extra premium), Gold, and Platinum plans, but they are not allowed on the Bronze plan [1]. Because premium is determined by the age of the eldest member covered, adding a dependent parent to a floater often costs more than an individual senior-citizen policy for that parent [4].

Credit for waiting periods served is granted only up to the sum insured of the previous policy, including its accrued no-claim bonus [1][2]. Any increase or excess in the sum insured is subject to fresh waiting periods on the incremental amount [1][2].

To continue newborn cover beyond 90 days, you must add the baby to the policy as a dependent and inform Aurora within 90 days of birth [1]. Doing so within this 90-day window is guaranteed-issue with no medical underwriting [1].

Aurora settles or rejects a complete reimbursement claim within 15 working days of receiving the last required document [1][2]. However, the archived 2024 rules state a deadline of 30 days from the last document [3].

Based on the provided sources, the Aurora Gold plan has no co-payment at all ages [1][4]. Additionally, the Aurora Silver and Bronze plans have no co-payment for insured members below the age of 60 [2][5].

You should buy the Gold plan, as it removes room-rent and ICU sub-limits [3] and covers dependent parents-in-law [1][4].

v2_rows.answer: You have 30 days from the date of discharge to submit a main reimbursement claim [1][2]. However, group claims have a submission window of 60 days from discharge [5]. Additionally, the archived 2024 rules indicate a 15-day deadline from the date of discharge [3].
The room rent limit on the Silver plan is 2% of the sum insured per day [3][4].
No, maternity cover is not available on the Bronze plan at any sum insured [1][2].

The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 36 months on retail and top-up/super top-up plans [3][5][7], and 24 months on the Aurora Senior Care plan for ages 60 and above [5]. Hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and cardiac conditions declared at the proposal stage carry a 36-month waiting period unless Aurora explicitly waives it in writing on the policy schedule [3].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days [1].
Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns as of 1 April 2026 [1].

Under the Aurora Gold plan, the no-claim bonus is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating to a maximum of 100% [1]. This bonus is not reduced by a claim, though it stops accumulating for that year only [1].
No, you cannot claim for IVF treatment, as infertility, assisted reproduction, and IVF are listed as permanent treatment-related exclusions [1].
The cataract surgery sub-limit on Gold is ₹75,000 per eye [1].

If you are not satisfied with the Stage 1 outcome or receive no response within 15 days, you can escalate the matter to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer [2]. If Aurora's final response remains unsatisfactory, or if they do not respond within 30 days of the original complaint, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [1].

For all plans, road ambulance cover is ₹5,000 per hospitalisation (road ambulance only) [1], [6]. Additionally, the Aurora Gold plan provides air ambulance cover of up to ₹2,50,000 per policy year, within India, on prior authorisation [5].

Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness, as required by the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 [1]. The 30-day initial waiting period applies, but no separate waiting period does [1].

The free-look period is 15 days from receipt of the policy document, or 30 days for policies sold through distance marketing [1][2]. It is defined as the window in which a new policy can be returned for a refund [3].
You get 150 wellness points for completing an annual health check-up [1].

A day-care procedure is a procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation due to technological advancement, and it is payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [3]. Out-patient treatment is not considered a day-care procedure [3].
A hospital must notify Aurora of an emergency admission for cashless within 24 hours of admission [1][5].
No, Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a Third Party Administrator (TPA) [1].
To qualify as a hospital under the policy, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or 15 in-patient beds elsewhere [1].

No, not everything will be paid [1][8]. Because you occupied a room at ₹15,000 per day while your Silver room-rent limit is 2% of the sum insured (₹10,000 per day), a proportionate deduction applies [1][2]. Consequently, everything tied to the room category is proportionately reduced, and you will pay ₹85,000 out of pocket, though pharmacy and consumables are not proportionately reduced [1][5][8].

Your mother can be added as a dependent parent on the Silver, Gold, and Platinum plans, but not on the Bronze plan [1]. On the Silver plan, she can be added at an extra premium [1]. Additionally, because the premium is determined by the age of the eldest member covered, adding a dependent parent to a floater often costs more than an individual senior-citizen policy, and advisers are required to present both options in writing before the sale [4]. Furthermore, if the eldest insured member is above 60 years at the time of policy commencement or renewal, a 10% co-payment applies to every claim on the Silver plan [8].

Credit for waiting periods served is granted only up to the sum insured of the previous policy, including its accrued no-claim bonus [1][2]. Any increase in sum insured, or the excess sum insured, is subject to fresh waiting periods [1][2].

To continue newborn cover beyond 90 days, you must add the newborn as a dependent by informing Aurora within 90 days of birth [1]. Adding the newborn within this 90-day window is guaranteed-issue with no medical underwriting [1].
